title: Waves (Sound & Light)
description: Properties of transverse and longitudinal waves, the electromagnetic spectrum, and sound.

notes.heading: Wave Properties
notes.body: All waves transfer energy without transferring matter. Key properties: Amplitude — maximum displacement from rest (related to intensity). Wavelength (λ) — distance between two adjacent peaks or troughs. Frequency (f) — number of complete waves per second, measured in Hertz (Hz). Period (T) — time for one complete wave (T = 1/f). Wave speed: v = fλ.

notes.heading: Transverse and Longitudinal Waves
notes.body: Transverse: particles oscillate at right angles to wave direction. Examples: light, water waves, all EM waves. Longitudinal: particles oscillate parallel to direction of travel, creating compressions and rarefactions. Example: sound waves. Sound cannot travel through a vacuum (needs particles); light can (travels at 3 × 10⁸ m/s).

notes.heading: The Electromagnetic Spectrum
notes.body: The EM spectrum is a family of transverse waves, all travelling at the speed of light in a vacuum. Order (increasing frequency): radio waves → microwaves → infrared → visible light → ultraviolet → X-rays → gamma rays. Applications: radio (communication), microwaves (cooking, satellites), infrared (heat sensors), visible light (sight), UV (sterilisation), X-rays (medical imaging), gamma rays (cancer treatment).

flashcards.definition: Number of complete waves passing a point per second, measured in Hertz (Hz).
Distance between two consecutive peaks (or troughs) of a wave.
Particles oscillate at right angles to the direction of wave travel.
Particles oscillate parallel to direction of wave travel, creating compressions and rarefactions.
Range of all EM waves ordered by frequency: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, UV, X-ray, gamma.

questions.stem: A wave has frequency 200 Hz and wavelength 2 m. What is its speed?
In which type of wave do particles vibrate at right angles to the direction of wave travel?
questions.explanation: Transverse waves have perpendicular particle oscillation.

questions.stem: Why can light travel through space (a vacuum) but sound cannot?
choices: Light has higher frequency than sound
Sound needs particles to vibrate, but space has no particles
Light is longitudinal, sound is transverse
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave needing a medium; a vacuum has no particles. Light is an EM wave.

questions.stem: Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum has the highest frequency?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays have the highest frequency and shortest wavelength.

questions.stem: Increasing the amplitude of a sound wave affects which property?
questions.explanation: Amplitude relates to energy; larger amplitude = louder sound. Pitch is determined by frequency.
